subject.title: cron: ghost runs recorded as ok when gateway is down (durationMs < 50ms)

question: Should this ghost-run fix use the linked PR's defaulted config/protocol/run-log warning surface, or be narrowed to a smaller runtime/log warning before landing?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the requested adjustable threshold and persisted warning shape affect operator config, generated protocol clients, UI, and docs, which needs maintainer product direction.

options.title: Refresh and settle linked PR
options.body: Resolve conflicts, remove unrelated churn, fix proof/docs gaps, and land the warning only after maintainers accept the config/protocol shape.

options.title: Narrow the diagnostic
options.body: Replace the linked PR with a smaller log-only or diagnostics-only warning if the new config/protocol field is not wanted.

options.title: Reject the heuristic
options.body: Close the warning direction only if maintainers decide fast `next-heartbeat` handoffs are expected and should not be surfaced as possible failures.

recommendation.title: Refresh and settle linked PR
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts, remove unrelated churn, fix proof/docs gaps, and land the warning only after maintainers accept the config/protocol shape.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron/gateway stability work makes this the best available routing owner for the product-shape decision.
